security_spec.violation_condition: QEMU models critical-error state via cpu_abort() at target/riscv/cpu_helper.c:2478, terminating the entire VM. Multi-hart systems lose all harts (not just the faulting one), and before termination, QEMU's timer device (CLINT/ACLINT mtime) and PMU counters may have already advanced beyond the point where the critical-error was detected, since the abort is reached only after counter read paths in the trap delivery sequence have executed. If QEMU later replaces cpu_abort() with a per-hart halt while leaving the timer device running, performance counters and timers would continue updating during the critical-error halt—a behavior the spec now explicitly labels UNSPECIFIED, creating a side channel where observing hart B's time/counter CSRs reveals that hart A entered critical-error and how long it has been halted.
security_spec.summary: QEMU terminates VM on critical-error via cpu_abort() but spec now leaves counter/timer updates UNSPECIFIED during this state; a future per-hart halt implementation that keeps counters running would leak critical-error timing information through shared timer/perf-counter CSRs accessible to other harts
